name: Kochariya-East Danuwar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog meds are wordlists only (Shackelford et al. 2018; van Driem 2001 survey pages); no grammar/phonology of Kochariya-East Danuwar found.

sources.citation: Mother Tongue Centre Nepal. 2024. 'Danuwar glossary' project post (Dudhauli, Sindhuli glossers entering words in FLEx).

sources.note: Nothing; used for identity only (Kochariya = Singoul Ward 1, Nijgadh, Bara; Danuwar = Chandanpur, Ranibas, Sindhuli).

Regmi, Ambika & Indresh Thakur. 2016. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Danuwar. Report submitted to Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 132 pp. (complete copy re-hosted by the Language Commission of Nepal, content id 10016)
sources.note: Nothing. Survey points include Bhaluwahi (Hatpate-6, Sindhuli) and Kachhadiya Tole (Nijgadh-4, Bara) = koch1253 area. Only phonological remark is second-hand (p.9, summarising Eppele et al. 2012): 'It is a non-tonal language. There are 29 consonant and 6 vowel phonemes in the language.'

sources.citation: Basnet, Yamuna. 2015. Tense and Aspect in English and Danuwar Languages: A Comparative Study. M.Ed. thesis, Faculty of English Education, Tribhuvan University. 75 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Danuwar of Hansposa-9, Sunsari; tense/aspect only.

sources.citation: Sapkota, Madhusudan. 2014. Danuwari matribhashi vidyarthiharule Nepali bhashako shabdochcharanma garne trutiharuko adhyayan [Errors in Nepali pronunciation made by Danuwari mother-tongue students]. M.Ed. thesis, Dept. of Nepali Language Education, Tribhuvan University. 66 pp. (Preeti-font PDF; converted to Unicode and read)
sources.note: Nothing. Danuwari speakers of Nipane, Hatpate and Sirthauli VDCs, eastern Sindhuli (= koch1253). Segment/word-level error analysis only (a/aa, retroflex/dental, j/jh, y/e, v/b, h-loss, prothetic i-); the word balaghat 'stress' never occurs.

sources.citation: Dahal, Shiv Kumari. 2012. M.Ed. thesis, Faculty of Nepali Language Education, Tribhuvan University. 64 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Kachhadiya (= Kochariya) Danuwar of Sarlahi; gender, number, agreement, case, sentence type, mood only.

sources.note: Describes Rai-Danuwar of Kavre (dhan1265), naming kachariya-danuvar as a separate dialect; 5.1.0 (p.292): 'Suprasegmentnye xarakteristiki v D.ja. ne issledovany' = suprasegmental characteristics have not been investigated. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Kuegler, Klaus P. & Doris Kuegler. 1974. Danuwar Rai Phonemic Summary. Kathmandu: SIL & INAS, Tribhuvan University. ix+91 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: HathiTrust digitized, search-only (in copyright); interlibrary loan
sources.note: Per sibling audit of the scanned (dhan1265): Dewas Rai variety (Makwanpur), not koch1253; no section on stress/accent; only passing remarks (p.75 emphasis = rising pitch + heavy stress + length; p.77 di- vs trisyllables differ in 'stress and rhythm'). No placement statement.
